anomalies.obs: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the FCC-side EEPROM U3 (24CW1280T-I_OT) has its SCL pin (1) wired to the global label I2C1_SCL_FCC, while its SDA pin (3) is wired to I2C2_SDA_FCC. The two serial-interface lines of the same device therefore sit on two different I2C buses.
anomalies.expected: An I2C device's SCL and SDA must be on the same bus. Every other I2C device on this board keeps the pair together: the PCA9685 U2 on this sheet uses I2C2_SCL_FCC + I2C2_SDA_FCC, the INA219 U1 on the Power sheet uses I2C2_SCL_FCC + I2C2_SDA_FCC, and the NAVC EEPROM U9 uses I2C1_SCL_NAVC + I2C1_SDA_NAVC. The FCC EEPROM should likewise have both lines on I2C2 (the FCC peripheral bus).

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals sheet, U3 24CW1280T-I_OT: pin 1 SCL -> label 'I2C1_SCL_FCC', pin 3 SDA -> label 'I2C2_SDA_FCC'
FCC Peripherals sheet, U2 PCA9685PW: pin 26 SCL -> 'I2C2_SCL_FCC', pin 27 SDA -> 'I2C2_SDA_FCC' (both on I2C2)
Component Table: 'FCC-side EEPROM | FCCPeripherals | 24CW1280T-I_OT'; Power distribution: '3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs'

anomalies.impact: The FCC EEPROM cannot be clocked by the MCU that drives its SDA bus (I2C2), so it is effectively unreachable and the FCC loses its non-volatile storage. The stray SCL connection also loads the I2C1 link bus (the FCC<->NAVC interconnect) with an extra device. The fix is to move the SCL label to I2C2_SCL_FCC.

parsed.summary: The build matches the spec on power, the dual-MCU split, sensors, PWM driver, flash and the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, but the FCC-side EEPROM U3 is drawn with SCL on the I2C1 bus and SDA on the I2C2 bus, splitting one I2C device across two buses and making it inoperable.
